priorReview.rationale: The current CLI accepts exactly --python and one explicit absolute local interpreter path. Re-read its full runtimeReceipts -> verifyImplementationBuild -> stableBytes flow. The Python bridge text, repository root and certification directory are fixed by this script; the bridge enumerates repository PROFILES and certification_result validates exchange identifiers against [a-z][a-z0-9_]{1,63}, profile identity, pinned SDK and independently trusted receipt hashes before returning rows. The later receipt path is therefore not a remotely chosen archive member. stableBytes validates canonical parents, an ordinary non-symlink single-link file, O_RDONLY/O_NOFOLLOW where available, and matching identities before/during/after the bounded read. The reported readSync argument is an opened descriptor rather than an unvalidated path string. A user selecting a malicious local Python executable already exercises the explicit local execution capability; this CLI is not an untrusted runtime selector exposed by the application. False positive for this exact reported path-traversal flow, not a claim that arbitrary interpreters are trusted.

priorReview.rationale: Re-read CLI arity/flag guard, runtimeReceipts and the complete Python bridge. Only --python plus one absolute executable path is permitted. The selected executable is canonicalized with realpath and checked as an ordinary file under a canonical parent. spawnSync receives an argument array containing fixed -I, -B, -c, fixed bridge code and the fixed repository root; shell:false, windowsHide, a 30-second timeout and a 2-MiB output limit remain explicit. Shell metacharacters in the selected path do not become shell syntax. Running the operator-selected local Python interpreter is the intended capability, not an attacker-supplied shell command. The service does not provide a remote route to this CLI selector. This is an individual false-positive determination for indirect command injection, not an assertion that malicious local executables would be safe.

priorReview.rationale: Independently inspected the distinct stableBytes openSync sink in the reported CLI -> interpreter output -> receipt exchange flow. The script derives repositoryRoot from its own module location and the certification directory is constant. Its fixed Python bridge obtains exchanges only from local PROFILES and accepts certification_result success, whose strict identifier/profile checks and approved receipt pins precede output. Receipt schema/hash comparison precedes the final local receipt read. openSync uses read-only flags with no-follow support, after canonical-parent and lstat regular-file/single-link checks, then verifies descriptor identity. It does not grant arbitrary write access as suggested by the generic finding. Explicit selection of the local Python executable is operator authority; no HTTP or signal input chooses it. This assessment covers the particular flagged open path, not all possible filesystem attacks.
